prerequisites: Master all knowledge acquired in 1st year courses, such as CALCULUS AND LINEAR ALGEBRA AND GEOMETRY. It is also recommended to attend class and maintain a continuous study habit for the course.

learning_outcomes.text: That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations
That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences

syllabus_topics: LINE INTEGRAL: Definitions.- Gradient of a scalar field. Properties.- Divergence of a vector field. Solenoidal field.- Curl of a vector field. Conservative field.- Laplacian of a scalar field.- Calculation of the line integral. -Conservative vector fields and path independence. -Green's Theorem.

SURFACE INTEGRALS: Area of a surface given in explicit and parametric form.- Surface elements.- Surface integral.- Calculation of surface integrals.- Stokes' Theorem.- Flux of a vector field.- Divergence Theorem or Gauss-Ostrogradski Theorem.

INTRODUCTION TO DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS: Definitions, fundamental concepts and notations.- Solutions. Type of solutions.- Classification of differential equations.- Origin and application of differential equations: Families of curves.

FIRST-ORDER DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS: Existence and uniqueness theorems for solutions.- Geometric interpretation.- Differential equations with separable variables and reducible to them.- Homogeneous equations and reducible to them.- Exact differential equations: Integrating factor.- Linear equations. Reducible to linear.- Orthogonal and isogonal trajectories.

HIGHER-ORDER LINEAR DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS: Introduction to higher-order linear differential equations.- Homogeneous linear equation. Vector treatment of the set of solutions.- Order reduction.- Second-order homogeneous linear equations with constant coefficients. Solution.- Complete second-order linear ODE. Solution: Variation of parameters method and method of undetermined coefficients.- Linear ODEs with variable coefficients: Euler's equation.- Other variable changes in linear equations with variable coefficients.- Applications: Vibrations in mechanical and electrical systems.

SYSTEMS OF ORDINARY DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS: Definition.- First-order homogeneous and non-homogeneous linear systems.- Linear systems with constant coefficients.- Autonomous system of two differential equations.- Phase diagram. Critical points.- Stability at a critical point.- Stability in homogeneous and non-homogeneous linear autonomous systems.

LAPLACE TRANSFORM: Definition.- Calculation of transforms of elementary functions.- Properties.- Inverse transform and transforms of derivatives.- Translation theorems.- Convolution product. Laplace transform of convolution product.- Application of the transform to the resolution of differential and integral equations and systems of linear differential equations.
NUMERICAL METHODS FOR SOLVING ODEs: Euler's method.- Taylor methods of order n.- Runge-Kutta methods. Runge-Kutta of order 4.

assessment_methods.method: Written test of theoretical-practical knowledge and problems on course content
Test on Numerical Methods content in ODEs and PDEs (theoretical and practical exercises)
